description.value: A real-time fMRI neurofeedback study examining modulation of craving-related BOLD responses and resting-state functional connectivity in patients with alcohol use disorder and healthy controls.

spans.text: The aim of the present project was to investigate the feasibility of rtfMRI neurofeedback to influence both neuronal responses and craving to addiction-related cues in patients with alcohol use disorder.

value: BOLD responses in circumscribed brain areas can be modulated with the aid of rtfMRI neurofeedback
these processes are related to decreased subjective craving ratings after neurofeedback sessions

functional differences regarding true rtfMRI could be enhanced compared to baseline in the sense that an improved down-regulation of hyper-connectivity in brain regions like the insular cortex, ACC or DLPFC may be of clinical relevance

spans.text: The main hypotheses were that BOLD responses in circumscribed brain areas can be modulated with the aid of rtfMRI neurofeedback and that these processes are related to decreased subjective craving ratings after neurofeedback sessions.
